title: Improving MPI Language Support Through Custom Datatype Serialization
problem: MPI only defines interfaces for C and Fortran, making it difficult for modern languages like Python, Julia, C++, and Rust to use MPI efficiently with their complex type systems. The existing derived datatype interface fails to handle types with multiple pointers or those requiring application-specific initialization, forcing applications to resort to complicated address manipulation or high overhead.
motivation: Exascale applications are increasingly being written in modern programming languages, so enabling efficient MPI support for these languages is critical for the HPC community.
method: The work proposes a new MPI datatype interface that gives applications direct control over buffer packing and wire representation. The authors built a prototype implementation and demonstrated it with three modern languages—Rust, Python, and C++—examining language-specific concerns and performance improvements.
key_novelty: A new MPI datatype interface enabling custom serialization and packing control for complex data types across modern programming languages.
contributions: Proposes a new MPI datatype interface for custom serialization and buffer packing
Provides prototype implementation supporting Rust, Python, and C++
Demonstrates language-specific concerns and performance improvements over existing approaches

metrics.other: improvements mentioned but not quantified in abstract
